newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Hokkaido Takushoku Bank to merge.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Hokkaido Takushoku Bank to merge.

text.p: Hokkaido Takushoku Bank, the tenth-largest commercial bank in Japan, has reached a basic agreement to merge with Hokkaido Bank Ltd, the Jiji news agency reported late Monday.
Hokkaido Takushoku has long been rumoured to be a merger candidate given its heavy burden of problem loans.
Jiji said the merger of the bank group, both based on Japan's northernmost main island of Hokkaido, would concentrate on being a regional powerhouse.
As part of the merger, Hokkaido Takushoku would give up its overseas operations, Jiji said.
Representatives of the two banks were not immediately available for confirmation of the report.
A senior official at Japan's Ministry of Finance said that he was aware that the two banks were in merger talks, but he said he could not confirm that a merger agreement had been reached.
Japan's plans to introduce a "Big Bang" financial reform package is expected to produce several mergers and takeovers in the country's overextended banking sector, industry analysts say.
Major Japanese banks are suffering from a heavy burden of problem loans after the collapse in the early 1990s of the economic bubble of inflated land prices.

Jiji said the merger would be announced on Tuesday with the larger Hokkaido Takushoku Bank being the surviving entity. It said that Sadamasa Kawatani, president of Hokkaido Takushoku, would become the chairman of the merged group while Hokkaido Bank President Tsuneo Fujita will be president.
The report did not give any details of the merger agreement.
